title: POC Weekly — Model priority matrix & emergency fallback plan
summary: Third weekly POC sync focused on choosing which model variants to prioritize for production pinning. Reviewed recent latency/cost regressions, discussed canary & emergency fallback criteria, and agreed on next steps to run targeted latency runs and share a trimmed benchmark CSV. Action items assigned for Redwood to produce rollback runbook and for ParcelShift to provide peak traffic traces.
action_items: Maya Chen; Send trimmed benchmark CSV (p95/p99 traces + token counts) to Nina; Due: 2025-06-19
Liam O'Connor; Produce emergency rollback runbook draft (canary steps + metrics triggers); Due: 2025-06-20
Nina Patel; Share 72h peak traffic traces and typical prompt length histogram; Due: 2025-06-18
Samir Gupta; Confirm VPC egress rules and KMS integration feasibility for Private deployment; Due: 2025-06-24
next_steps: Redwood to run two targeted latency sweeps (short/long context) on the preferred quantized variant and share results
Customer to decide initial pin set by Friday, June 20
Schedule follow-up tabletop rollback drill next week (30 minutes)
transcript:
Header: 
Date: 2025-06-16 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (SE), Priya (SE), Erik (ParcelShift CTO), Nina (Lead ML Eng), Samir (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto): quick notes — model ranking, latency spike on 6/14, agree canary + emergency fallback.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off — short agenda, 1) results from the last week, 2) pick model priority, 3) what our rollback / emergency fallback looks like.
[00:22] Erik: Yeah thanks Maya, quick context, we saw a p95 spike on Tuesday during a large batch ingest, caused some timeouts for customers on mobile, so it's top of mind.
[00:45] Nina: And just to add, the prompt lengths changed for a subset of flows, average token count went up from ~120 to ~300 for certain user journeys. We flagged that in the metrics.
[01:10] Liam: Right, that aligns with the KV cash — I mean KV cache — behavior we suspected; the longer context increases cache pressure and causes more GPU mem churn on the quantized variant.
[01:35] Priya: Quick correction, not necessarily mem churn, could be increased decoder steps causing kernel scheduling delays. But yes, workload shift.
[01:58] Maya: Cool, quick poll — model candidates we tested last week: redwood-g-3-gray (the latest 8-bit quant), rwood-slim-1 (server-optimized fp16), and an older large fp32 baseline. Which variant are we leaning to pin?
[02:20] Nina: From accuracy standpoint, redwood-g-3-gray matched baseline on our eval set for NLU intents, minor regressions on long-form summarization but acceptable.
[02:45] Samir: But the latency on that quantized variant had p99 at 3.8s during peak, compared to 2.2s on rwood-slim-1. Cost delta was ~30% lower on the quantized one.
[03:08] Erik: So it's a tradeoff: cost vs tail-latency. We care about p99 for customer-facing features. If p99 is high, escalations happen.
[03:33] Liam: We proposed a tiered pin: pin rwood-slim-1 for customer-facing endpoints, and use redwood-g-3-gray for background/async tasks. That gives a cost hedge.
[03:55] Nina: That could work. Need to know how easy it is to route by endpoint — can we do per-route pinning in the console?
[04:10] Priya: Yes, per-route pinning exists, we can set pins per API key or route, and set soft fallback to a cheaper variant if the pinned one fails. There is also a canary window option.
[04:32] Erik: What about automatic fallback policies? If the pinned model hits a latency SLO for 2 consecutive minutes, can we fail-over automatically?
[04:52] Maya: There's a policy engine; we usually recommend a two-tier policy: 1) short grace window (90s aggregated) then switch to soft fallback for X% traffic, 2) if persistent, route 100% to fallback and alert on-call. We can codify exact thresholds.
[05:18] Nina: I want the thresholds tied to concrete metrics — p95 and p99 and error rate. p99 > 2.5s for 3 minutes should trigger the partial shift.
[05:40] Liam: Noted. We'll draft triggers: p99>2.5s for 3m -> 20% shift to fallback; p99>3.5s for 5m -> 100% shift. Those numbers are draft.
[06:05] Samir: Also need a circuit-breaker if errors increase, e.g., >=2% 5xx.
[06:22] Maya: Good. Let's talk rollback runbook. Liam, can you summarise what you'd include in a minimal emergency rollback doc?
[06:35] Liam: Sure. Step 0: validate monitoring streams (traces, p99, errors). Step 1: initiate canary rollback on 10% traffic to pinned baseline, watch metrics for 5m. Step 2: if no improvement, expand to 50% for 10m; Step 3: if no improvement revert 100% and open postmortem. Include play-by-play CLI/API commands to pin/unpin via the version gateway, and a list of stakeholders with on-call links.
[07:03] Priya: We'll also include rollback simulation steps: a dry-run on staging and a tabletop drill with a 30-min window.
[07:20] Erik: That sounds good. On the model choice again, the team is leaning to the tiered approach but concerned about complexity. How many pins are too many?
[07:36] Nina: Ideally 2-3 variants: primary for live, secondary for async/batch, and a degraded fallback (smaller footprint) for emergency. We don't want combinatorial pins per route.
[07:55] Maya: Agreed. We'll recommend a small catalog: Primary (rwood-slim-1), Secondary (redwood-g-3-gray), Emergency-slim (rwood-nano-0).
[08:12] Samir: What's rwood-nano-0 for quality? Might be aggressive for fallback on user-facing flows.
[08:26] Liam: It's meant as a last-resort degraded path — short responses, higher hallucination risk but lower latency. Use only for non-critical flows.
[08:40] Nina: Ok let's map endpoints to these tiers; I'll take the mapping action.
[09:00] Maya: Great. Next, anomalies — we saw a spike on 6/14. Liam, any insight from the tests you ran?
[09:12] Liam: We ran a reproducer and saw the p99 climbs when average prompt length >220 tokens and concurrency > 120 req/s on a single VM. The quantized kernel seems to hit a scheduler lock more often. There's also a chance our batching window settings were too aggressive.
[09:38] Priya: We should tune the batching guard: reduce max batch delay from 30ms to 12ms for the real-time endpoints to reduce tail. That will slightly increase token cost but brings p99 down.
[09:56] Nina: Can we measure cost impact? We need the numbers to present to execs.
[10:05] Maya: We'll run a cost/latency sweep and produce a small CSV with p95/p99/cost per 1M tokens for the two settings.
[10:18] Erik: Also, what about Dedicated vs Hosted? The POC has been on Hosted with reserved pool — but private is on the roadmap for compliance. If we go Dedicated, does that change fallback behavior?
[10:36] Priya: Dedicated gives you more predictable throughput and you can control autoscaling windows; fallbacks still work but you might want to pre-reserve warm capacity for the fallback models. For Private on-prem there're additional networking rules and KMS concerns.
[10:52] Samir: For Private we need audit logs, SOC2 attestations. Are those available now?
[11:00] Maya: Yes Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and supports KMS/HSM integrations; we'll share the security pack after this call.
[11:12] Nina: Great. Back to pin mechanics — what's the easiest path to pin by route and have a soft fallback? Is there API or only Console?
[11:25] Liam: Both. You can set pins via the Redwood API (version gateway) and set a fallback policy object. We'll paste example curl commands in the runbook.
[11:40] Maya: Ok moving on — let's capture the acceptance criteria for final pin set. Nina, what would make you comfortable to sign a pin?
[11:52] Nina: Three things: 1) Verified p99 under 2.5s for 48h at expected traffic mix, 2) rollback plan documented and tested, 3) cost delta documented for exec approval.
[12:10] Erik: Timeline is tight — we want to start pinning a small set by next Friday.
[12:20] Maya: That's doable. We'll target the short latency sweeps and the runbook this week.
[12:30] Samir: Quick question — what about model warmup? Should we pre-warm KV cache after deploy?
[12:40] Priya: Yes, plan a warmup script that sends representative prompts at low QPS for ~10 minutes to populate prefix cache. We'll include a script sample.
[12:53] Nina: Please also document the warmup for each variant — quantized variants may need longer warmup for KV structures.
[13:06] Liam: Noted.
[13:12] Maya: Any blockers on instrumentation? We need consistent tracing to detect p99 and error spikes.
[13:19] Samir: We have OpenTelemetry in front of the API gateway, but some spans are being dropped during peak; we'll investigate and share logs.
[13:32] Erik: For the cost numbers, can Redwood provide per-token billing estimates for each variant at the observed token distribution?
[13:45] Maya: Yes, we'll compute per-variant cost per 1M tokens given your histogram. Please send the histogram.
[13:55] Nina: Will do.
[14:00] [--- Meeting moves into deep dive on canary thresholds ---]
[14:10] Liam: For canary we recommend dynamic step-up: start at 5% for 5m, then 20% for 10m, 50% for 15m with checks — if at any point metrics degrade, rollback. This limits blast radius.
[14:35] Erik: Are these steps configurable per-route?
[14:39] Priya: Yes. The policy engine supports per-route policy objects.
[14:46] Nina: What about automation? Can we tie the canary to an SLO and have it auto-promote if SLO holds?
[14:55] Liam: You can. The promotion rules can be SLO-based; we'll share a sample policy.
[15:06] Maya: Ok quick pause — action items recap: Redwood runs latency sweeps, posts CSV; Liam drafts rollback runbook; ParcelShift sends traffic histogram; Samir checks tracing.
[15:25] Nina: One more question — are there any known compatibility issues between rwood-slim-1 fp16 and our current tokenizer pipeline? We swapped to a new tokenizer on May and want to make sure tokenization differences don't shift accuracy metrics.
[15:45] Liam: It shouldn't, but we saw minor tokenization boundary differences once with a whitespace normalization. We'll include a tokenizer diff checklist in the eval notes.
[16:05] Erik: If we pin then later unpin to a different variant, how do we preserve user experiences stored in the cache? Is there a KV migration concern?
[16:22] Priya: The prefix cache isn't portable between model variants; switching will cold-start users, which is why warmup plus gradual canary matters. We'll document expected cold-start penalty.
[16:40] Samir: Also mention tool calling — some of our flows use function calling and need deterministic structured output. Are certain variants worse at that?
[16:55] Nina: In our eval rwood-g-3-gray had slightly more structured output drift on complex tool calls, which is why we prefer rwood-slim-1 as primary for user-facing tool calling.
[17:12] Maya: Great. Let's schedule a 30-minute tabletop drill next Thursday to run through the rollback. Everyone ok with that?
[17:25] Erik: Yes.
[17:30] Maya: Alright, any last comments?
[17:35] Nina: None from me.
[17:37] Samir: I'm good.
[17:40] Maya: Thanks all — we'll email the notes and the artifacts.
[17:45] [Meeting ends; final quick notes]

Post-call notes:
- Redwood to include example version-gateway API snippets, warmup scripts, and the draft rollback runbook in a shared drive link (will send in follow-up).
- Customer to provide traffic histogram and confirm endpoints that are considered "customer-facing" vs "background".

References shared: "benchmark_sweep_0614.csv" (Redwood internal link), "security_pack_v2.pdf" (Redwood security), playbook template link to runbook.md

End of transcript.
